question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` remain limited to caller-supplied client `tool_calls`, or should OpenClaw add an explicit redacted mode for internal tool-call telemetry?
rationale: Current source, tests, docs, and the latest release define the existing client-tool contract; exposing internal tool calls would change the API and security boundary rather than repair a confirmed regression.

options.title: Keep Current Contract
options.body: Keep `tool_calls` for caller-supplied HTTP tools and point internal-tool visibility to Gateway/session diagnostics or observability issues.

options.title: Design Opt-In Telemetry
options.body: Sponsor a new redacted diagnostic/API mode with scopes, docs, and tests before exposing internal tool-call metadata.

options.title: Fold Into Observability Work
options.body: Route this need into the broader tool-call observability or AI diagnostics issues if maintainers want one telemetry contract instead of a Chat Completions special case.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Contract
recommendation.body: Keep `tool_calls` for caller-supplied HTTP tools and point internal-tool visibility to Gateway/session diagnostics or observability issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged tool-protocol PR was landed with this account's follow-up commit and proof comment, and the question is now about the product/security boundary around that contract.
